library.name: Customer Document Exchange Architecture
library.scope: Target design for customer case document retrieval

brief:
# Fictional customer document exchange design brief

Northbridge Advice is an invented organisation used solely to demonstrate SABSA authoring. The target service accepts customer case documents and supports retrieval by the owning customer or a currently assigned case worker. No deployment, approval, test result, legal obligation or actual performance is asserted.

The business outcome is trustworthy document exchange with confidential and attributable retrieval. A misused staff session is the illustrative threat scenario. The proposed service measures attribution completeness with a target of 100% and reconciles decisions each business day. The Customer Operations Director sponsors the outcome; the Customer Service Owner owns the proposed policy and operational assessment.

The design separates identity authentication, case assignment, authorisation, release enforcement and audit delivery. The gateway obtains an allow decision and commits a minimal evidence record before releasing bytes. Indeterminate authorisation and a full buffer deny retrieval. Decision identifiers support audit replay and duplicate detection. A fictional gateway reference implementation illustrates the component boundary.

The following detailed specifications and narrative decisions are part of this fictional brief. They are design inputs, not claims about a real organisation.

## BD-001 — Trustworthy customer document exchange

- statement: Customers can exchange case documents without unauthorised disclosure or loss of accountability.
- owner: Customer Operations Director

The fictional Northbridge Advice service accepts confidential case documents through a customer portal. A document can affect a time-sensitive service decision, so both confidentiality and demonstrable attribution matter. The target architecture protects customer submission and staff retrieval while keeping the customer journey understandable.

The business outcome is a trustworthy exchange, rather than the procurement of a particular product. The service sponsor expects each security design choice to connect to this outcome. Availability targets for the wider customer platform remain outside this example and need a separate architecture decision.

## RO-001 — Unauthorised retrieval of customer documents

- kind: threat
- statement: A stolen staff session could expose documents belonging to customers outside the assigned case.
- likelihood: Scenario for design evaluation; not a measured likelihood
- impact: Disclosure and loss of customer confidence
- owner: Customer Operations Director
- attributes: BA-001

The relevant scenario starts with a valid but misused staff session. Authentication alone cannot establish that a particular document should be released. The design therefore evaluates case assignment and the requested document for each retrieval.

This is an illustrative risk scenario. No incident, quantified risk assessment or accepted residual risk is asserted. Session theft detection and endpoint protection are dependencies to be evaluated by the wider platform team.

## BA-001 — Accountable confidentiality

- definition: Customer documents are released only to an entitled customer or assigned case worker, and the decision is attributable.
- metric: Percentage of document retrieval decisions with subject, case, decision and correlation identifiers
- measurement: Reconcile gateway retrieval decisions against the case-access audit stream each business day
- target: 100% of retrieval decisions have the required attribution fields
- owner: Customer Service Owner
- drivers: BD-001

Accountable confidentiality combines a disclosure boundary with an observable business measure. A successful retrieval must identify the subject and the customer case; a denied retrieval must retain the same decision context without exposing document content in the audit record.

The target is a proposed design criterion for the fictional service. The example does not claim that the criterion is currently achieved. Sampling and evidence retention decisions belong to the service owner and require validation during a pilot.

## CO-001 — Authorise and evidence every document retrieval

- statement: Evaluate current case entitlement for every retrieval and record a content-free, attributable decision before releasing document bytes.
- attributes: BA-001
- risks: RO-001

The objective addresses RO-001 by preventing a general staff session from acting as a blanket document entitlement. It also creates the evidence needed to assess BA-001.

The design fails closed when entitlement cannot be established. Audit delivery failure handling is a separate acceptance concern: the component design buffers a bounded decision record before release and signals backlog growth to operations. The permissible backlog and recovery objective remain proposed values to be agreed in the pilot.

## DM-001 — Customer case processing domain

- scope: Customer document intake and retrieval within the fictional case service
- authority: Customer Service Owner
- objectives: CO-001

The Customer Service Owner is the proposed authority for case-access rules in this domain. The identity platform supplies authenticated subject identifiers; the case system supplies current assignment. Neither dependency independently authorises document release.

External identity assurance and workforce lifecycle administration are outside this domain boundary. Their contracts must be reviewed before deployment; this example records the dependency without asserting their effectiveness.

## SS-001 — Case-bound document authorisation

- description: Evaluate subject, case assignment and requested document, then return an attributable allow or deny decision.
- objectives: CO-001
- domain: DM-001
- policies: PL-001

The service receives a subject identifier, a case identifier, a document identifier and a correlation identifier. It obtains current case assignment through an authenticated internal interface. The response includes the decision, policy revision and a stable reason code.

A deny result does not reveal whether the document exists. An indeterminate dependency response becomes a deny result with an operational reason code. The retrieval gateway releases document bytes only after an allow decision is recorded in the local evidence buffer.

This logical contract is technology independent. Timeout budgets, buffer limits and deployment topology are specified in the physical and component viewpoints.

## PL-001 — Case-specific document access policy

- statement: The proposed target policy allows retrieval only for the owning customer or a currently assigned case worker; all other requests are denied.
- owner: Customer Service Owner
- objectives: CO-001
- services: SS-001

This proposed policy applies to the fictional document exchange boundary. The policy is a design input awaiting the service owner's approval, not a binding rule adopted by a real organisation.

Support access and emergency access are excluded from ordinary case-worker entitlements. A separate documented decision is required before either access path can be introduced. Denied requests produce a reason code suitable for support investigation without including document text.

## SM-001 — Gateway enforcement with bounded decision buffer

- description: A retrieval gateway calls the authorisation service and writes the decision to a local bounded buffer before serving document bytes.
- services: SS-001

The gateway is the document release point. Direct customer access to the object store is not part of the proposed design. The gateway validates request identifiers and forwards only the minimum decision context to the authorisation service.

A bounded local write-ahead buffer separates the decision path from asynchronous audit transport. When the buffer cannot accept a record, retrieval is denied and the gateway raises an operational signal. Recovery replays committed records using the decision identifier to support duplicate detection.

The deployment pilot must demonstrate that a gateway restart cannot release bytes for an unrecorded decision. Capacity and recovery behaviour require measured acceptance evidence before production use.

## SC-001 — Document gateway reference implementation

- product: Fictional document-gateway 0.1 reference implementation
- version: 0.1
- mechanisms: SM-001

The component specification is deliberately vendor neutral. The reference gateway exposes a retrieval endpoint and contains an authorisation adapter, a bounded evidence buffer and an object-store reader. The object-store reader is invoked only after the allow decision has been durably accepted by the buffer.

Configuration includes the authorisation endpoint, trust anchors, maximum buffer capacity, replay rate and operational alert destination. Values are environment-specific and must be supplied through the deployment configuration process. No production addresses or access material are included in this example.

Verification exercises allow, deny, stale assignment, unavailable authorisation, full buffer and restart/replay cases. The acceptance record links test inputs and observed decisions to CO-001. A passing test run has not been asserted by this fictional specification.

## ME-001 — Retrieval decision attribution completeness

- metric: Retrieval decisions with all attribution fields divided by total retrieval decisions
- data_source: Gateway decision log reconciled with the case-access audit stream
- frequency: Each business day
- target: 100%
- threshold_action: Investigate any missing attribution record and assess whether retrieval should be restricted
- owner: Customer Service Owner
- attributes: BA-001
- services: SS-001

The collector reconciles decision identifiers rather than comparing document content. Missing and duplicate records are reported separately. Records with an absent subject, case, policy revision or correlation identifier fail the completeness check.

A daily result is evidence about attribution completeness, not proof that every authorisation policy decision was correct. Policy correctness requires separate case-based review and negative-path tests. The service owner reviews both evidence streams before making an assurance claim.

## EV-001 — Daily attribution reconciliation report

- evidence_type: Reconciliation report with decision counts and unresolved discrepancies
- location: Illustrative service evidence repository; deployment location not yet assigned
- collector: Service assurance collector
- measures: ME-001

The proposed report records the collection period, collector version, source counts, matched decision identifiers, duplicates and unresolved discrepancies. It excludes document bodies and uses case identifiers only where needed for authorised investigation.

Retention duration, access permissions and disposal controls require an explicit service decision before use. This example identifies the required evidence structure without inventing an approved retention policy.

## SO-001 — Review attribution discrepancies

- metric: Open retrieval-attribution discrepancies
- frequency: Each business day
- owner: Customer Service Owner
- threshold_action: Assign an investigator, contain affected retrieval paths if needed, and track corrective action to closure
- attributes: BA-001
- services: SS-001
- measures: ME-001

The service analyst reviews ME-001 and opens a discrepancy record for each unmatched decision. The investigator identifies whether the problem lies in collection, transport, policy enforcement or source reconciliation, retaining the decision identifier and relevant deployment revision.

The service owner decides on temporary retrieval restrictions when the evidence no longer supports accountable confidentiality. Recovery includes replay, reconciliation and an explicit closure decision. Repeated discrepancies feed the component backlog and the architecture review.

## component viewpoint decisions

This fictional target architecture describes gateway component behaviour and verifiable failure handling for Northbridge Advice. SC-001 specifies the fictional gateway reference component that realises SM-001. The component contract describes interfaces, configuration responsibilities and verification cases; it does not claim a real product has been built or tested. The document is a worked example for architecture authoring and review. It asserts no approval, implementation result or legal applicability.

This viewpoint serves component engineers and implementation reviewers. Its purpose is to define component specifications, engineering conventions and verification instructions for the selected realisation. The scope is customer case document retrieval. Wider platform resilience, workforce lifecycle administration and emergency access remain outside the demonstrated design and require separate decisions.

BD-001 establishes the need for trustworthy document exchange. RO-001 considers misuse of a staff session to access another customer case. BA-001 and CO-001 connect that scenario to measurable accountability and a case-specific release decision. The source brief describes a hypothetical service; it is not evidence of an actual incident or of compliance with a regulation.

The Customer Operations Director sponsors the business outcome and owns the illustrative risk scenario. The Customer Service Owner owns the proposed access policy and reviews the evidence for accountable confidentiality. For gateway component behaviour and verifiable failure handling, engineering and operations contributors supply design and execution evidence; the service owner retains the decision on readiness. These are proposed example responsibilities, not real organisational appointments.

The architecture uses retrieval-attribution completeness as a proposed measure, with a target of 100% of decisions carrying the defined identifiers. A daily reconciliation report is the intended evidence. It does not prove policy correctness by itself; case-based policy review and negative-path verification provide complementary evidence. No measured value or successful execution is claimed.

No exception is approved in this example. If a real design cannot meet CO-001, the author must identify the affected case, residual exposure, proposed compensating measures, owner and review date. The publication workflow preserves an unresolved decision rather than treating the absence of an exception record as acceptance.

A real change record should identify the changed source, impacted stable IDs, rationale and acceptance evidence. Changes to authored narrative invalidate the snapshot approval in the same way as changes to element specifications.

The canonical source for this example is 00-sources/example-brief.md. Terms such as customer, case worker, retrieval decision and attribution are defined in that brief. References to element identifiers identify architecture dependencies, not external obligations. No external standard text, legal interpretation or licensed business attribute taxonomy is reproduced.

The component contains an authorisation adapter, bounded evidence buffer and object-store reader. The invariant is that the reader cannot release bytes until an allow decision has been accepted by the evidence buffer. Configuration is versioned with the deployment and reviewed as part of the release evidence.

Implementation work must preserve request correlation through policy evaluation, local evidence acceptance and audit replay. Environment-specific endpoints, trust anchors, capacities and alert destinations remain deployment inputs. They are not embedded as sample production configuration in this document.

Verification includes allow, deny, stale assignment, service unavailability, buffer saturation and restart/replay. Each case records the policy revision, decision identifier and observed release behaviour. Known limitations include the absence of measured capacity results and a completed implementation; these remain release blockers for a real deployment.

## BP-001 — Customer case document retrieval

- description: A customer or assigned case worker requests a case document and receives it only after an attributable case-access decision.
- owner: Customer Service Owner
- drivers: BD-001

The process starts when a requester selects a document within a case. The service authenticates the requester, resolves case assignment, records the access decision and releases the document only when allowed. A denied request follows a support path that does not disclose document existence.

The outcome is a controlled customer interaction with an investigable decision record. Wider case resolution and customer communications are outside this process description.

## ET-001 — Authenticated document requester

- population: Customers and case workers with an authenticated service session
- owner: Customer Service Owner
- objectives: CO-001
- domains: DM-001

The requester is identified by a stable subject identifier. Authentication establishes the subject; it does not by itself establish entitlement to a case document. The logical access service combines that identity with current case assignment.

The entity model distinguishes customer ownership from workforce assignment without assuming either category grants unrestricted document access.

## ET-002 — Document retrieval service

- population: Service instances acting as the controlled document release point
- owner: Platform Engineering Lead
- objectives: CO-001
- domains: DM-001

The retrieval service receives a request context and enforces the authorisation decision before returning document bytes. Its service identity is distinct from the end-user subject retained in the decision record.

Operators manage the service configuration; ordinary platform administration does not imply a business entitlement to customer documents.

## IF-001 — Case document retrieval request

- information: Subject, case, document and correlation identifiers; document bytes only after an allow decision
- protection: Authenticate the requester, bind the request to current case entitlement and record the decision before release
- owner: Customer Service Owner
- source_entity: ET-001
- target_entity: ET-002
- objectives: CO-001
- services: SS-001

The request carries the minimum identifiers needed for a case-specific decision. The response contains document bytes only after successful authorisation and evidence acceptance. A denied response uses a stable reason code and does not reveal whether the requested object exists.

Audit evidence contains identifiers and decision context, not document bodies. Protection of the transport and endpoint trust is validated in the deployment design.

## PC-001 — Authorise, record and release

- trigger: A requester asks to retrieve a case document
- sequence: Validate request context; obtain current entitlement decision; accept decision evidence; release bytes only for allow
- review_cycle: Review when policy or gateway behaviour changes
- owner: Customer Service Owner
- services: SS-001

The logical sequence makes decision evidence part of the retrieval contract. An indeterminate entitlement result ends the interaction with a deny decision. Evidence-buffer rejection also prevents release.

Audit transport follows local acceptance and may replay after restart. The physical design establishes the durability and capacity assumptions behind this sequence.

## DS-001 — Case document object repository

- technology: Private object repository; deployment product not selected
- data_classes: Customer case documents and object identifiers
- information_flows: IF-001
- mechanisms: SM-001

The repository stores customer documents behind the retrieval gateway. It is not a customer-facing access endpoint. The gateway supplies the authorised retrieval path while the repository maps a case-bound document identifier to the stored object.

Storage placement, encryption configuration, recovery policy and administrative access controls are deployment decisions still requiring review. The example does not invent approved settings for them.

## PR-001 — Handle evidence-buffer saturation

- procedure: Deny new retrievals that cannot record evidence; signal operations; investigate backlog; reconcile recovered decisions before restoring ordinary service
- owner: Customer Service Owner
- policies: PL-001
- mechanisms: SM-001

The procedure begins when the gateway cannot accept another decision record. New retrieval attempts are denied rather than served without attribution. The service analyst checks transport health and buffer status, preserving the decision identifiers needed for recovery.

Recovery replays committed records and reconciles them with the audit stream. The service owner reviews unresolved discrepancies before declaring the incident closed. No actual response-time achievement is asserted.

## DF-001 — Case document object metadata

- schema: case_id, document_id, object_revision and content_reference; deployment schema revision to be assigned
- encoding: UTF-8 for textual identifiers; document payload retains its original media encoding
- data_stores: DS-001

The metadata separates business identifiers from the physical content reference. A document revision is explicit so that evidence can identify which object version was retrieved. Textual identifiers use UTF-8 and preserve their canonical values.

The final storage schema, validation limits and migration rules require implementation review. This example records the proposed information contract without supplying a production schema.

## EP-001 — Gateway document retrieval interface

- endpoint: Logical /cases/{case_id}/documents/{document_id} retrieval endpoint
- protocol: Authenticated HTTPS; deployment trust profile to be reviewed
- components: SC-001

The interface accepts a retrieval request and returns either an authorised document response or a denial with a stable reason code. Correlation is retained across authorisation and evidence acceptance. The endpoint shape is illustrative and is not a deployed address.

The component verification plan checks identifier validation, denial behaviour and interruption before byte release. Concrete protocol versions and trust settings are deployment inputs requiring approval.

## RM-001 — Validate the proposed retrieval design

- current_state: Fictional target specification; no implementation or measured evidence is claimed
- target_state: Pilot evidence demonstrates attributable retrieval and fail-closed error paths
- owner: Customer Service Owner
- target_date: To be agreed before a real delivery commitment
- acceptance_evidence: Reviewed allow, deny, unavailable-service, buffer-full and restart/replay results with reconciliation report
- objectives: CO-001
- components: SC-001

The transition action is to implement a controlled pilot and collect evidence against CO-001. Its first decision is whether the interface and evidence contracts are sufficiently precise for engineering. A subsequent review assesses observed failure handling and attribution completeness.

A real delivery plan must assign dates, resources and approval authority. This fictional action deliberately records those commitments as unestablished rather than inventing a schedule.

entries.title: Trustworthy customer document exchange

fields.statement: Customers can exchange case documents without unauthorised disclosure or loss of accountability.

entries.body:
The fictional Northbridge Advice service accepts confidential case documents through a customer portal. A document can affect a time-sensitive service decision, so both confidentiality and demonstrable attribution matter. The target architecture protects customer submission and staff retrieval while keeping the customer journey understandable.

The business outcome is a trustworthy exchange, rather than the procurement of a particular product. The service sponsor expects each security design choice to connect to this outcome. Availability targets for the wider customer platform remain outside this example and need a separate architecture decision.

entries.title: Unauthorised retrieval of customer documents

fields.statement: A stolen staff session could expose documents belonging to customers outside the assigned case.
fields.likelihood: Scenario for design evaluation; not a measured likelihood
fields.impact: Disclosure and loss of customer confidence

entries.body:
The relevant scenario starts with a valid but misused staff session. Authentication alone cannot establish that a particular document should be released. The design therefore evaluates case assignment and the requested document for each retrieval.

This is an illustrative risk scenario. No incident, quantified risk assessment or accepted residual risk is asserted. Session theft detection and endpoint protection are dependencies to be evaluated by the wider platform team.

entries.title: Accountable confidentiality

fields.definition: Customer documents are released only to an entitled customer or assigned case worker, and the decision is attributable.
fields.metric: Percentage of document retrieval decisions with subject, case, decision and correlation identifiers
fields.measurement: Reconcile gateway retrieval decisions against the case-access audit stream each business day
fields.target: 100% of retrieval decisions have the required attribution fields

entries.body:
Accountable confidentiality combines a disclosure boundary with an observable business measure. A successful retrieval must identify the subject and the customer case; a denied retrieval must retain the same decision context without exposing document content in the audit record.

The target is a proposed design criterion for the fictional service. The example does not claim that the criterion is currently achieved. Sampling and evidence retention decisions belong to the service owner and require validation during a pilot.

entries.title: Authorise and evidence every document retrieval

fields.statement: Evaluate current case entitlement for every retrieval and record a content-free, attributable decision before releasing document bytes.

entries.body:
The objective addresses RO-001 by preventing a general staff session from acting as a blanket document entitlement. It also creates the evidence needed to assess BA-001.

The design fails closed when entitlement cannot be established. Audit delivery failure handling is a separate acceptance concern: the component design buffers a bounded decision record before release and signals backlog growth to operations. The permissible backlog and recovery objective remain proposed values to be agreed in the pilot.

entries.title: Customer case processing domain

fields.scope: Customer document intake and retrieval within the fictional case service

entries.body:
The Customer Service Owner is the proposed authority for case-access rules in this domain. The identity platform supplies authenticated subject identifiers; the case system supplies current assignment. Neither dependency independently authorises document release.

External identity assurance and workforce lifecycle administration are outside this domain boundary. Their contracts must be reviewed before deployment; this example records the dependency without asserting their effectiveness.

entries.title: Case-bound document authorisation

fields.description: Evaluate subject, case assignment and requested document, then return an attributable allow or deny decision.

entries.body:
The service receives a subject identifier, a case identifier, a document identifier and a correlation identifier. It obtains current case assignment through an authenticated internal interface. The response includes the decision, policy revision and a stable reason code.

A deny result does not reveal whether the document exists. An indeterminate dependency response becomes a deny result with an operational reason code. The retrieval gateway releases document bytes only after an allow decision is recorded in the local evidence buffer.

This logical contract is technology independent. Timeout budgets, buffer limits and deployment topology are specified in the physical and component viewpoints.

entries.title: Case-specific document access policy

fields.statement: The proposed target policy allows retrieval only for the owning customer or a currently assigned case worker; all other requests are denied.

entries.body:
This proposed policy applies to the fictional document exchange boundary. The policy is a design input awaiting the service owner's approval, not a binding rule adopted by a real organisation.

Support access and emergency access are excluded from ordinary case-worker entitlements. A separate documented decision is required before either access path can be introduced. Denied requests produce a reason code suitable for support investigation without including document text.

entries.title: Gateway enforcement with bounded decision buffer

fields.description: A retrieval gateway calls the authorisation service and writes the decision to a local bounded buffer before serving document bytes.

entries.body:
The gateway is the document release point. Direct customer access to the object store is not part of the proposed design. The gateway validates request identifiers and forwards only the minimum decision context to the authorisation service.

A bounded local write-ahead buffer separates the decision path from asynchronous audit transport. When the buffer cannot accept a record, retrieval is denied and the gateway raises an operational signal. Recovery replays committed records using the decision identifier to support duplicate detection.

The deployment pilot must demonstrate that a gateway restart cannot release bytes for an unrecorded decision. Capacity and recovery behaviour require measured acceptance evidence before production use.

entries.title: Document gateway reference implementation
entries.body:
The component specification is deliberately vendor neutral. The reference gateway exposes a retrieval endpoint and contains an authorisation adapter, a bounded evidence buffer and an object-store reader. The object-store reader is invoked only after the allow decision has been durably accepted by the buffer.

Configuration includes the authorisation endpoint, trust anchors, maximum buffer capacity, replay rate and operational alert destination. Values are environment-specific and must be supplied through the deployment configuration process. No production addresses or access material are included in this example.

Verification exercises allow, deny, stale assignment, unavailable authorisation, full buffer and restart/replay cases. The acceptance record links test inputs and observed decisions to CO-001. A passing test run has not been asserted by this fictional specification.

entries.title: Retrieval decision attribution completeness

fields.metric: Retrieval decisions with all attribution fields divided by total retrieval decisions
fields.data_source: Gateway decision log reconciled with the case-access audit stream
fields.threshold_action: Investigate any missing attribution record and assess whether retrieval should be restricted

entries.body:
The collector reconciles decision identifiers rather than comparing document content. Missing and duplicate records are reported separately. Records with an absent subject, case, policy revision or correlation identifier fail the completeness check.

A daily result is evidence about attribution completeness, not proof that every authorisation policy decision was correct. Policy correctness requires separate case-based review and negative-path tests. The service owner reviews both evidence streams before making an assurance claim.

entries.title: Daily attribution reconciliation report

fields.evidence_type: Reconciliation report with decision counts and unresolved discrepancies
fields.location: Illustrative service evidence repository; deployment location not yet assigned

entries.body:
The proposed report records the collection period, collector version, source counts, matched decision identifiers, duplicates and unresolved discrepancies. It excludes document bodies and uses case identifiers only where needed for authorised investigation.

Retention duration, access permissions and disposal controls require an explicit service decision before use. This example identifies the required evidence structure without inventing an approved retention policy.

entries.title: Review attribution discrepancies

fields.threshold_action: Assign an investigator, contain affected retrieval paths if needed, and track corrective action to closure

entries.body:
The service analyst reviews ME-001 and opens a discrepancy record for each unmatched decision. The investigator identifies whether the problem lies in collection, transport, policy enforcement or source reconciliation, retaining the decision identifier and relevant deployment revision.

The service owner decides on temporary retrieval restrictions when the evidence no longer supports accountable confidentiality. Recovery includes replay, reconciliation and an explicit closure decision. Repeated discrepancies feed the component backlog and the architecture review.

entries.title: Customer case document retrieval

fields.description: A customer or assigned case worker requests a case document and receives it only after an attributable case-access decision.

entries.body:
The process starts when a requester selects a document within a case. The service authenticates the requester, resolves case assignment, records the access decision and releases the document only when allowed. A denied request follows a support path that does not disclose document existence.

The outcome is a controlled customer interaction with an investigable decision record. Wider case resolution and customer communications are outside this process description.

entries.title: Authenticated document requester

fields.population: Customers and case workers with an authenticated service session

entries.body:
The requester is identified by a stable subject identifier. Authentication establishes the subject; it does not by itself establish entitlement to a case document. The logical access service combines that identity with current case assignment.

The entity model distinguishes customer ownership from workforce assignment without assuming either category grants unrestricted document access.

entries.title: Document retrieval service

fields.population: Service instances acting as the controlled document release point

entries.body:
The retrieval service receives a request context and enforces the authorisation decision before returning document bytes. Its service identity is distinct from the end-user subject retained in the decision record.

Operators manage the service configuration; ordinary platform administration does not imply a business entitlement to customer documents.

entries.title: Case document retrieval request

fields.information: Subject, case, document and correlation identifiers; document bytes only after an allow decision
fields.protection: Authenticate the requester, bind the request to current case entitlement and record the decision before release

entries.body:
The request carries the minimum identifiers needed for a case-specific decision. The response contains document bytes only after successful authorisation and evidence acceptance. A denied response uses a stable reason code and does not reveal whether the requested object exists.

Audit evidence contains identifiers and decision context, not document bodies. Protection of the transport and endpoint trust is validated in the deployment design.

entries.title: Authorise, record and release

fields.trigger: A requester asks to retrieve a case document
fields.sequence: Validate request context; obtain current entitlement decision; accept decision evidence; release bytes only for allow
fields.review_cycle: Review when policy or gateway behaviour changes

entries.body:
The logical sequence makes decision evidence part of the retrieval contract. An indeterminate entitlement result ends the interaction with a deny decision. Evidence-buffer rejection also prevents release.

Audit transport follows local acceptance and may replay after restart. The physical design establishes the durability and capacity assumptions behind this sequence.

entries.title: Case document object repository

fields.technology: Private object repository; deployment product not selected
fields.data_classes: Customer case documents and object identifiers

entries.body:
The repository stores customer documents behind the retrieval gateway. It is not a customer-facing access endpoint. The gateway supplies the authorised retrieval path while the repository maps a case-bound document identifier to the stored object.

Storage placement, encryption configuration, recovery policy and administrative access controls are deployment decisions still requiring review. The example does not invent approved settings for them.

entries.title: Handle evidence-buffer saturation

fields.procedure: Deny new retrievals that cannot record evidence; signal operations; investigate backlog; reconcile recovered decisions before restoring ordinary service

entries.body:
The procedure begins when the gateway cannot accept another decision record. New retrieval attempts are denied rather than served without attribution. The service analyst checks transport health and buffer status, preserving the decision identifiers needed for recovery.

Recovery replays committed records and reconciles them with the audit stream. The service owner reviews unresolved discrepancies before declaring the incident closed. No actual response-time achievement is asserted.

entries.title: Case document object metadata

fields.schema: case_id, document_id, object_revision and content_reference; deployment schema revision to be assigned
fields.encoding: UTF-8 for textual identifiers; document payload retains its original media encoding

entries.body:
The metadata separates business identifiers from the physical content reference. A document revision is explicit so that evidence can identify which object version was retrieved. Textual identifiers use UTF-8 and preserve their canonical values.

The final storage schema, validation limits and migration rules require implementation review. This example records the proposed information contract without supplying a production schema.

entries.title: Gateway document retrieval interface

fields.protocol: Authenticated HTTPS; deployment trust profile to be reviewed

entries.body:
The interface accepts a retrieval request and returns either an authorised document response or a denial with a stable reason code. Correlation is retained across authorisation and evidence acceptance. The endpoint shape is illustrative and is not a deployed address.

The component verification plan checks identifier validation, denial behaviour and interruption before byte release. Concrete protocol versions and trust settings are deployment inputs requiring approval.

fields.target_date: To be agreed before a real delivery commitment

component.executive-summary: This fictional target architecture describes gateway component behaviour and verifiable failure handling for Northbridge Advice. component.purpose-scope: This viewpoint serves component engineers and implementation reviewers. Wider platform resilience, workforce lifecycle administration and emergency access remain outside the demonstrated design and require separate decisions.
component.business-risk-context: BD-001 establishes the need for trustworthy document exchange. RO-001 considers misuse of a staff session to access another customer case. BA-001 and CO-001 connect that scenario to measurable accountability and a case-specific release decision. Evidence collection records the collection period and collector revision. Retention, access and disposal rules require an explicit service decision before deployment; no retention duration is invented here.
service-management.improvement: Repeated discrepancies inform corrective engineering and architecture review. Improvement actions must identify the affected objective, the proposed change and acceptance evidence. Operational assurance is a continuing assessment of the service, not a one-time inference from the presence of a report.

component.how: SC-001 specifies the fictional gateway reference component that realises SM-001. The component contract describes interfaces, configuration responsibilities and verification cases; it does not claim a real product has been built or tested.

component.where: The component boundary contains the authorisation adapter, bounded evidence buffer and object-store reader. External services are represented by explicit interfaces; no production endpoint or host is embedded in the specification.
component.when: Component verification covers allow, deny, stale assignment, unavailable service, full buffer and restart/replay. Execution budgets and capacity thresholds require measured pilot results before a real release decision.

contextual.why: The viewpoint supports BD-001 through BA-001 and CO-001, addressing the RO-001 unauthorised retrieval scenario. These relationships identify a design rationale, not an assertion of implemented effectiveness.
contextual.how: The customer document journey begins with submission and ends with an attributable retrieval. Customer Operations owns the outcome; platform and identity services are dependencies. The architecture scope excludes wider platform availability and workforce lifecycle controls.
